companyIntro.name: Quantis Capital
companyIntro.mission: Give mid-sized businesses institutional-grade financial planning, credit and compliance discipline.
companyIntro.culture: Numbers must tie out and every assumption must be written down. Analysts are expected to defend their model line by line.

projectBackground.name: Equity Research — Northern Packaging plc
projectBackground.context: Northern Packaging trades at 15x earnings. Is it fairly valued against peers and its cash flows?

manager.name: Jonas Brandt
manager.note: I need a view, a valuation range and what would make you wrong.

assignment.title: Value Northern Packaging and recommend
assignment.brief: Discount cash flows, compute multiples, compare peers in Excel and write the recommendation.

documents.name: Forecast Cash Flows
documents.note: Free cash flow: 100, 110 and 121 over three years; discount rate 10%.

documents.name: Market Data
documents.note: Price 45; EPS 3; market cap 800; debt 300; cash 100; EBITDA 125.

documents.name: Peer Table
documents.note: Three peers with price, EPS, EV and EBITDA.

tasks.title: Present Value
tasks.prompt: Discount cash flows of 100 (year 1), 110 (year 2) and 121 (year 3) at 10%. What is the total present value?
tasks.reasoning: DCF values future cash at today's money.
tasks.mistake: Summing undiscounted cash gives 331, which overstates value.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: P/E Ratio
tasks.prompt: Share price 45 and EPS 3. What is the P/E?
tasks.mistake: A low P/E is not automatically cheap.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: EV/EBITDA
tasks.prompt: Market cap 800, debt 300, cash 100, EBITDA 125. What is EV/EBITDA?
tasks.mistake: Using market cap alone ignores leverage.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Discount Rate Sensitivity
tasks.prompt: A small rise in the discount rate cuts value sharply for a long-duration business. Why?
options: Distant cash flows are discounted more heavily
tasks.reasoning: Value of later cash is more sensitive to the rate.
tasks.mistake: A single-point estimate hides the range.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Peer Multiples (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Calculate P/E (D = B / C) and EV/EBITDA (G = E / F) for the three peers and upload.
tasks.reasoning: Peer multiples frame whether the target looks cheap or expensive.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Recommendation
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence recommendation on Northern Packaging.
tasks.modelAnswer: I recommend a hold. At 15x earnings and 8x EV/EBITDA the shares trade in line with peers (9x, 10x, 4x), and the DCF of about 273 on three years of cash flow supports the current price only if growth continues. The main risk is a higher discount rate or weaker volume, which would cut value materially. I would add on a pullback toward 12x earnings, and revisit after the next results.
tasks.reasoning: A good recommendation gives a view, valuation evidence, key risk and a trigger.
tasks.mistake: A number without a view isn't a recommendation.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Cheap Stock
caseStudy.background: An analyst bought a company at 6x earnings because it looked cheap. A debt-heavy balance sheet and falling margins meant earnings collapsed and the shares halved.
caseStudy.challenges: Only P/E was used; leverage ignored.
caseStudy.solution: Quantis requires EV-based multiples, a balance sheet check and a downside case for every recommendation.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Cheap can be cheap for a reason.

quiz.q: The case study lost money because:

prompts: Which assumption drives your valuation most?
What would prove your recommendation wrong?
